label: 1.1.2-opus-high
messages: /tokenwise:route implement a feature from a written spec, about 12 files
/tokenwise:route review a six-file diff in a repo I know well

result:
- Phase: implementing a feature from a written spec, about 12 files
- Model and effort: `/model sonnet` then `/effort medium`
- Boundary: if the spec was written in this session, save it to a file, `/clear`, then switch. On most models, switching model or effort mid-conversation makes the whole current context get processed again. `/context` shows how big that is. This answer stays in your context until your next `/clear`, so it costs least right before one.
- Delegate: send test runs, log reading and any reading of the codebase beyond the files you're editing to subagents. Set `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` so they don't run on the session model. At 12 files, work in slices with `/clear` between them if context grows past what the next slice needs.
- Done when: the project's test suite passes with no test file edited except tests the spec calls for, and lint is clean (`npm run lint` or equivalent).
- You give up: some reasoning headroom when the spec is ambiguous or the change reaches past the files it names. On the bench, sonnet at medium passed every run at 17% of the cost of opus at xhigh. That evidence is from `claude-sonnet-5` on a small test project.
- Escalate when: sonnet skips files, doesn't run tests or stops mid-task. That's a lack of effort, so raise it (`/effort high`, then `xhigh`). If it finishes but gets the logic wrong with the spec in context, it didn't know enough, so switch to `/model opus` at `medium`, then `xhigh`. Make either change at a `/clear` boundary.

- Phase: review a six-file diff in a repo you know well
- Model and effort: `/model opus` then `/effort low`. This matches the bench case directly. On a six-file diff, opus at low found all five planted defects in 3 turns. Opus at high found the same five in 13 turns and cost 3.3x as much. The evidence comes from `claude-opus-5`, which is what `opus` resolved to on 8 September 2026.
- Boundary: `/clear` first, then switch. If you switch on a warm context instead, your whole current context gets re-processed. `/context` shows how big that is. This answer also stays in your context until your next `/clear`, so it costs least if you route just before one.
- Delegate: nothing. You can hold six files in one context, and handing them to a subagent would just add a summary step between you and the diff.
- Done when: every finding has a file:line and an input that makes it fail, and each one has been checked against the diff.
- You give up: some coverage on subtle problems that cross files, since low effort runs fewer tool calls and less thinking. The bench showed no loss on this size of diff. Sonnet costs less but missed one defect in two runs of three at high effort, so dropping to Sonnet is the bad trade.
- Escalate when: the review skips files, finds nothing in a part of the diff you know is risky, or says something is fine without checking it. Those mean it didn't try hard enough, so raise to `/effort high` on opus. Also go to high if the diff turns out larger or less familiar than you expected.
